newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ad association outraged at billboard ruling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ad association outraged at billboard ruling.

text.p: A leading U.S. advertising association warned on Thursday that cities seeking to restrict billboard advertising of tobacco and spirits should not take comfort in an unexpected ruling by a federal appeals court upholding such a ban for the city of Baltimore.
On Wednesday, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit in Richmond, Virginia, upheld Baltimore's bans on tobacco and alcohol advertising on outdoor billboards that may be seen by minors.
The 2-to1 ruling upholds a court decision rendered last year permitting the ban.
That decision was set aside by the U.S. Supreme Court in July when it asked the lower court to reconsider after striking down a liquor advertising ban in Rhode Island in May.

"I caution other municipalities thinking of imposing advertising restrictions -- you will still have to meet the difficult test imposed by the Supreme Court on commercial speech," Nancy Fletcher, president and chief executive of the Outdoor Advertising Association, said in a statement.

The Baltimore ordinance limits advertising of tobacco and alcoholic beverages to billboards adjacent to Interstate highways or within certain commercial zones in an attempt to discourage underage consumption of the products.
"The best possible balance between protecting children and protecting freedom of speech can be reached only if all parties work closely together on a voluntary basis," the statement said.
